How long does a technical SEO audit take?

Technical SEO audits vary enormously in scope, and the right number for you depends on factors we will walk through below. There is a lot of nuance here, and practitioners disagree, so please read the whole thing before drawing conclusions. Many teams also wonder whether they should run the audit themselves first.

Background and history

Search engines have crawled the web for three decades, and audit tooling has evolved alongside them. Early crawlers were simple. Modern ones are not. This history matters for understanding the tooling landscape in 2026.

Common variations in practice

Some teams audit a single page. Others audit a whole domain, an international subtree, or an archive of several million URLs. Crawl budgets, staging access and log availability all constrain the answer.

Factors that change the duration

Site size is the obvious factor. Render time matters. Whether you have server logs, whether staging is blocked by a password, and whether JavaScript has to execute before the content exists all add time.

The direct answer

A technical SEO audit of a 500-page marketing site takes 4 to 8 hours; a 50,000-URL site takes 2 to 4 weeks with two engineers and log access.

The short version is that the crawl itself is rarely the bottleneck. Review, prioritisation and sign-off are.
